issues.description: The problem statement and UML indicate Animal has a single attribute 'name' and students (see the commented Main) are expected to construct animals with a single String name. However, the solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute on Animal and provides constructors (Animal, Seal, Pig, Goat) that require both (String name, int age). This mismatch between the specified UML/description/template usage and the solution's constructors will confuse students and prevent them from matching the provided example usage in Main or the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructors consistent with the problem specification and template Main. Either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute from Animal and change all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) to accept only a single String name (and update solution code accordingly), which matches the UML and the commented example in Main; or (B) explicitly update the problem statement/UML and the template Main to document and use the additional 'age' attribute (e.g., show constructors with (String name, int age) and state the Animal has an age). Option A is recommended to preserve the current UML and template usage.

issues.description: Constructor/signature mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the problem statement and template expect classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) with constructors that initialize only the 'name' attribute (single String parameter), but the solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute and constructors taking (String name, int age). This inconsistency changes the public API students must implement/use (Main in the template calls one-arg constructors) and will confuse or prevent direct mapping from the problem/template to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to remove the extra 'age' attribute and change subclass constructors to single-argument constructors that only take 'name' (so they match the problem description and the template Main usage), or (B) update the problem statement and template to document and use the additional 'age' attribute and two-argument constructors (String name, int age) everywhere. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template for minimal student confusion.
